# Generation 007B execution

Generation 007B uses the Generation 007R supervisor. It does not run as one shard. A worker process owns one batch and exits. Completed items and batch receipts stay on disk, so a killed terminal does not discard finished work.

Scientific root: `constraint-lab/generated/generation-007b/`.

Preflight root: `constraint-lab/generated/generation-007b-preflight/`.

Smoke root: `constraint-lab/generated/generation-007b-smoke/`.

All three are gitignored. The frozen counts are in `constraint-lab/docs/generation-007b-work-count.md`.

`python -m rs_constraint_lab run` on this analysis is refused. The command to use is `generation007b`.

## Commands

From `constraint-lab/`:

```bash
python -m rs_constraint_lab generation007b plan
python -m rs_constraint_lab generation007b benchmark
python -m rs_constraint_lab generation007b smoke
python -m rs_constraint_lab generation007b preflight
python -m rs_constraint_lab generation007b start
python -m rs_constraint_lab generation007b status
python -m rs_constraint_lab generation007b status --watch 5
python -m rs_constraint_lab generation007b stop
python -m rs_constraint_lab generation007b restart
python -m rs_constraint_lab generation007b verify --require-complete
python -m rs_constraint_lab generation007b merge
```

`restart` is `start` on the same root. Completed items are not solved again.

`run-next` executes one batch and returns, with `--max-wall` defaulting to 60 seconds. `run-batches --count 5` executes five batches and returns. `supervise` runs until the plan is complete or stopped. Start that through `scripts/start-generation-007b.sh`, which returns after the supervisor has its own session.

`benchmark` measures the two-level pair-point item and writes `plan/batch-policy.json`. Until that file exists, each batch contains one item. The count is `floor(45 / p90)`, reduced while `count * p90 > 60` or `count * max > 100`. The watchdog stays 120 seconds. Smoke and preflight use their own roots. Copy `plan/batch-policy.json` into those roots after their plans exist. The measurement below is the copy source.

Measured on this machine on 2026-10-12, nine pair-point samples, numeric threads pinned to 1.

| Kind | p50 | p90 | max | items per batch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pair point | 0.290s | 0.315s | 0.315s | 142 |
| target singleton | 0.290s | 0.315s | 0.315s | 142 |
| target composition | not timed | not timed | not timed | 1 |
| control composition | not timed | not timed | not timed | 1 |

The target-singleton row uses the pair-point samples. It was not timed as its own kind. Composition stays at one item per batch.

The two-level reference gap on that run was 0, below `1e-10`. The match tolerance stays `1e-8`.

An atomic item is one canonical two-level control at one `(m_off, m_on)`, one rho, and one alphabet. It returns both singleton passage directions. The planner reads stored points and requests the next stencil. It does not call the kernel.

## Watching another terminal

Linux / WSL:

```bash
python -m rs_constraint_lab generation007b status --watch 5
tail -n 30 -f constraint-lab/generated/generation-007b/progress/progress.log
```

`status.json` is `constraint-lab/generated/generation-007b/progress/status.json`. The supervisor writes it when it starts, before the first heartbeat interval, and rewrites it on every heartbeat. `running_batches` has one row for each live worker: `batch_id`, `worker_pid`, `items`, `started_at`, `elapsed_seconds`, `watchdog_seconds`. `current_batch_id` remains the first live worker.

PowerShell, not executed on this Linux host:

```powershell
Get-Content .\constraint-lab\generated\generation-007b\progress\progress.log -Tail 30 -Wait
```

## Background start and stop

```bash
constraint-lab/scripts/start-generation-007b.sh
constraint-lab/scripts/stop-generation-007b.sh
constraint-lab/scripts/watch-generation-007b.sh
```

PowerShell equivalents are `start-generation-007b.ps1`, `stop-generation-007b.ps1`, and `watch-generation-007b.ps1` in the same directory. They were written for Windows. They were not executed on this Linux host. Native PowerShell validation is not claimed. That is not a blocker for the Linux scientific run.

`stop` asks the supervisor to finish the current batch, write `STOPPED`, and release the lock. A hard kill is recovered by the next start: valid items remain, and a batch without a receipt is scheduled again for the items that were not published.

A second live supervisor is refused. A lock whose process is gone is recovered and logged.

## What a batch is allowed to do

A normal batch targets 30–60 seconds. The watchdog is 120 seconds. The supervisor heartbeats at least every 10 seconds, including while a worker is still inside a solve. Two workers is the default. Each worker sets the numeric libraries to one thread.

On timeout the supervisor kills the worker process group, keeps published items, and splits the unfinished items. A single item that times out twice after the first attempt is quarantined. Other items continue.

Profiles:

```text
smoke       one logical problem, its coarse grid, adaptive cap 250, no composition
preflight   15 logical problems, representation and cost only
census      42 problems, then composition, then the robustness probes
```

Smoke and preflight do not schedule composition. The census schedules composition only for calibrations whose status is `represented`. `unresolved_at_cap` and unrepresented calibrations stay in the merge and do not receive composition or robustness items.

## Planner corrections before the census

Three corrections were made after the first smoke and the first preflight. They do not change the frozen selection rule or the tolerance.

- A named nominal of zero uses Generation 7 `log_distance`. The selector does not divide by that nominal.
- Newton starts only after both log10 widths are at most 0.05. A subdivision stencil that is already stored does not promote a wide basin to Newton.
- A missing Jacobian sample requests a durable point. It does not mark the basin exhausted.

An uncaught supervisor exception is written to `last_error` before the process exits. The state name remains `STOPPED`.

The corrected preflight is the one recorded in Pass 2 of `docs/generation-007b-design-passes.md`.

## Census close

The census root is `generated/generation-007b`. Its scientific reading is `reports/generation-007b-two-level-pair-face-control.md`. The machine-readable rows are `reports/generation-007b-tables.json`, rendered from `generated/generation-007b/merge/summary.json`. `generated/` stays gitignored.

`verify --require-complete` accepts a Generation 007B calibration whose `status` is `represented`, `unrepresented`, or `unresolved_at_cap`. Generation 7 still requires `convergence_status`. Merge rows for 007B are keyed by `calibration_id`, because one target can have more than one live face. The scalar-erasure state-shape join reads `generated/generation-007/merge/summary.json` and does not refit that control.

The census supervisor started at `2026-10-12T12:45:38Z` and its last activity is `2026-10-12T14:19:04Z`. Status is `COMPLETE`. Items are 4,539 / 4,539. Calibrations are 42 / 42. Unresolved calibrations, timeouts, retries, quarantines, and `last_error` are 0. Receipts are 196. There was no resume and no stale-lock event on this root. `cache_hits` and `cache_misses` in the status file are 0 because the 007B counter returns those fields as zero. They are not a kernel-cache measurement.

# Generation 007B work-count freeze

Frozen before the representability census. Counts come from `build_problems` on `experiments/specs/generation-007b.json`, not from prose. `tests/test_v07b.py` checks the primary row.

The census does not start until this file exists and `generation007b benchmark` has measured the two-level item. Batch size is chosen from that measurement. Generation 7's 142-item multiplier batch is not reused.

## Primary census

```text
logical calibration problems          42
unique two-level control structures    4
unique target singleton expressions   20
coarse-grid points per structure      81
initial atomic items                 344
```

`344 = 4 × 81 + 20`. The coarse axis is `1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1, 1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000`. Zero-boundary points are not in this initial count. They are requested only when a basin's best stored point sits on a positive-domain edge.

The 42 problems share 4 control structures. A `(structure, m_off, m_on, rho, alphabet)` evaluation is stored once and reused. Named grades change `Delta_T`, so the 42 residual problems stay distinct.

## Adaptive cap

```text
maximum adaptive points per logical calibration    250
```

The cap counts points first requested by that calibration. A point already stored for the same structure is free. One scheduler step requests at most 9 new points. If the next stencil does not fit in the remaining cap, the step requests none of it and the calibration becomes `unresolved_at_cap`. Coarse-grid points do not count as adaptive.

```text
worst-case adaptive items, primary       42 × 250 = 10500
worst-case primary items, including grid          10844
```

The expected adaptive count is not known until the preflight. The planning range, if one or two basins converge, is about 20–80 new points per problem. That range is not a cap and not a measurement.

## Preflight

Representability and cost only. No composition and no `M_I` or `M_G`.

```text
logical preflight problems            15
unique structures in the preflight     4
unique preflight target expressions    8
initial preflight atomic items       332
```

`332 = 4 × 81 + 8`. The preflight uses its own root, `constraint-lab/generated/generation-007b-preflight/`. Items are not copied from the census root. Because all 4 structures are included, the preflight coarse grid is the census coarse grid.

The 15 problems are every live face at polarity `absent` for `prohibit/prohibit`, `strong_suppress/strong_suppress`, `strong_favour/strong_favour`, and `strong_suppress/strong_favour`, plus every live face at polarity `present` for `prohibit/prohibit`.

Preflight adaptive worst case is `15 × 250 = 3750` points, plus the 332 initial items.

## Robustness, after the primary census is terminal

Six represented primary problems, at `rho3 = 1/2` and `rho3 = 2`, in two modes: held parameters, and a separate recalibration. Alphabet sensitivity is not scheduled.

```text
robustness problems                         6
unique structures among those problems      3
unique target expressions                   5
recalibration logical problems        6 × 2 = 12
recalibration coarse pair points      3 × 2 × 81 = 486
recalibration target singletons       5 × 2 = 10
recalibration adaptive cap           12 × 250 = 3000
```

Held probes add one pair point, one target singleton, one target composition, and one control composition at each new rho for each represented robustness problem. Unrepresented and `unresolved_at_cap` primaries do not schedule composition or robustness.

## Measured batch

Measured on this machine on 2026-10-12. Nine two-level pair-point solves, three repeats of three multiplier pairs, numeric threads pinned to 1. The same samples are the target-singleton policy. Composition items stay at one per batch until they are timed on their own. The count is `floor(45 / p90)`, and this measurement did not need a further reduction.

```text
pair_point p50     0.290 s
pair_point p90     0.315 s
pair_point max     0.315 s
items per batch    142
```

`142 × 0.315 s ≈ 45 s` of kernel time. The watchdog remains 120 seconds.

The two-level numerical reference on the same run has maximum absolute passage-gap `0` against the scalar pair-face at `(m_off, m_on) = (1, m)` and against condition erasure at `(m, m)`. That is below `1e-10`. The singleton tolerance stays `1e-8`.

## Disk and wall clock

Generation 7 item files were about 110 KB because each one stores length-1024 committor vectors. A 007B pair point does the same. The worst-case primary grid, the adaptive caps, composition for a small solution family, and the robustness caps are on the order of 15,000 item files, or about 1.7 GB, if every cap is reached.

Kernel-time sketch at the measured p90 and two workers, excluding process start and the atomic write:

```text
census coarse grid, 344 items                 about 1 minute
census adaptive, 20–80 points × 42            about 2–9 minutes
census adaptive, cap on every problem         about 28 minutes
preflight coarse grid, 332 items              about 1 minute
preflight adaptive cap, 15 × 250              about 10 minutes
```

The 20–80 point range is still a planning range. The preflight replaces it with a measured adaptive count before the census is interpreted. Composition and robustness are scheduled only after the primary calibrations are terminal, so their wall clock is added after that, not hidden inside the coarse grid.

# Independent hypergraph

Generation 3 adds one relation and does not add a place, a clock, or an entity-state channel.

## Slots

At `N = 3` the entities are `A`, `B`, and `C`, stored as `0`, `1`, and `2`. The four independent bits are:

```text
bit 0    AB     (0, 1)
bit 1    AC     (0, 2)
bit 2    BC     (1, 2)
bit 3    ABC    (0, 1, 2)
```

`ABC` present does not imply `AB`, `AC`, or `BC`. `AB ∧ AC ∧ BC` does not imply `ABC`. The labelled state space is the 4-dimensional Boolean hypercube: 16 states, four toggles from every non-halting state.

`S_3` fixes the triple and permutes the three pairs. The coarse classes are the pairwise isomorphism type crossed with the triadic bit. At `N = 3` the pairwise isomorphism type is the pair-edge count, so there are eight classes: empty, one pair, wedge, and triangle, each with the triad absent and present. States are not grouped by the total number of present relations. Empty pairs plus the triad is not the same class as one pair and no triad.

## Axes

Relation order `O` is the maximum cardinality of an independently existing relation. Generation 3 has `O = 3`.

Constraint arity `A` is the number of distinct entities named by the constraint. `form(0-1-2)` has `A = 3` with no other condition.

Geometric dimension stays `G = 0`. There is no embedding.

State-space dimension `S` keeps its existing meaning: finite channels other than the binary incidence of a named relation. The triadic bit is relational incidence. It is not counted in `S`. Generation 3 has `S = 0`, `H = 0`, and `L = 0`.

## Baseline

The primary baseline gives every slot toggle weight 1, including the triad. Formation and dissolution are symmetric. `rho3` is the relative baseline weight of the triadic toggle. The primary census uses `rho3 = 1`. The values `1/2` and `2` are a sensitivity check inside the same shards, not a second census.

## Grammar

Conditions may read a pair present or absent, or the triad present or absent. Count literals are refused in this grammar so they cannot treat the triad bit as another pair. The cross-order class of a constraint is `P->P`, `P->T`, `T->P`, `T->T`, or `mixed`.

## Comparison with the pairwise grammar

An edge-only rule on this kernel is not the Generation 1b kernel. The triad toggle is a fourth event. The comparison is the pairwise conditional jump kernel: at each triad bit, renormalise the three pair weights. Under `rho3 = 1`, an edge-only rule's two jump kernels equal the Generation 1b kernel of the same edge grammar.

Reducibility is stated only inside the Generation 1b `N = 3`, `K ≤ 3`, cardinalities `{1, 2, 3}`, structural-simple, pairwise-edge index, plus the unconstrained pairwise baseline. A miss against that index is `OUTSIDE_SEARCHED_PAIRWISE_GRAMMAR`, not a claim of absolute irreducibility.

## What this file does not decide

Simplicial face-closure is a different semantics. It is not executed here. Whether forming a 2-simplex creates absent faces, whether formation is prohibited until the faces exist, whether deleting a face deletes the simplex, and whether simplex dissolution is independent of face dissolution are questions for a later design note. None of those rules is compiled into these 16 states.

# Inquiry modes

Two modes of inquiry are legitimate in this laboratory. Generation 007B uses one of them. It documents the other and does not execute it.

## MODE A — discriminating experiment

This is the current mode.

Question form:

```text
What specific ambiguity remains?
What is the smallest controlled experiment that distinguishes the live explanations?
```

It emphasises:

```text
matched controls
predeclared observables
confound removal
bounded inference
```

A discriminating experiment freezes the ontology, the observable, the tolerance, and the selection rule before the comparison it is meant to inform. Representation, composition, state shape, selectivity, and complexity stay separate reports. They are not collapsed into one pass/fail judgement.

Pass and fail remain available for software tests, CI, verification, and explicit engineering requirements.

## MODE B — open relational exploration

This is a future mode. It is not executed in 007B.

Question form:

```text
What happens if we introduce this relation/constraint/process?
What structures emerge?
What changes when another element is added?
What recurrent patterns or transitions appear?
What does the accumulated trajectory suggest?
```

In this mode there is no scientific failure in the ordinary sense.

Unexpected outcomes are observations that redirect exploration.

The intellectual loop is:

```text
exploration
→ observation
→ inference
→ coherence comparison
→ revised exploration
```

This is compatible with the broader Relational Substrate methodology.

Generation 007B does not switch into Mode B. Mode B stays a future research fork.

## Reproducibility requirement for Mode B

When Mode B is eventually used, it must still be reproducible.

Any exploratory stochastic journey must preserve:

```text
initial state
random seed(s)
proposal sequence
accepted/rejected events
constraint additions/removals
parameter changes
intermediate states
observables
branch decisions
agent rationale / research question at each branch
```

The entire exploration should be replayable.

A stochastic exploratory path may be contingent.

It must not be opaque.

## Epistemic principle for a future exploratory run

When that mode is used:

```text
The absence of an expected phenomenon is an observation, not a failed experiment.
```

```text
Multiple causes are not automatically a defect; they are part of the relational structure to be disentangled later if useful.
```

```text
The purpose is directional information and coherence accumulation, not repeated binary hypothesis verdicts.
```

This does not weaken reproducibility. It changes the question being asked.

## Event-sourced exploratory journey

A future exploratory engine must make the entire journey reconstructible:

```text
experiment version
initial state
constraints at each step
proposal source
random seed
random draw
chosen event
state transition
observables before/after
agent-selected next perturbation
reason for perturbation
```

The final output should be analysable as a path, not merely as an endpoint.

Generation 007B documents this requirement. It does not implement the exploratory engine.

## Fork, not a change of the current question

If the discriminating-control programme reaches diminishing returns, a later branch may ask "What happens if...?" rather than "Does X pass this test?"

A possible future experiment should:

1. Begin from a minimal state/constraint grammar.
2. Allow bounded additions, removals, and modifications of relational constraints.
3. Run replayable stochastic trajectories.
4. Record every change and every random choice.
5. Observe emergent organisation, dissolution, transition, memory, boundary, routing, and repair. Those outcomes are not hard-coded.
6. Let observations determine the next exploratory perturbation.
7. Compare accumulated patterns for global coherence. A pass/fail status is not assigned at each step.

That fork is not part of the 007B execution.

## Generation 8 executes Mode B

Generation 8 is the first laboratory execution of Mode B. Generations 1 through 7B remain Mode A records. Their reports are historical evidence and are not reinterpreted by editing them.

Generation 8 asks:

```text
What happens when higher-order relational context is allowed to participate in an evolving stochastic relational system, and what recurrent structures, routes, transformations, and context dependencies actually appear?
```

The governing loop is:

```text
exploration
→ observation
→ inference
→ coherence comparison
→ revised exploration
```

A completed trajectory has no scientific pass or fail. Unexpected behaviour is an observation.

Scientific language for Generation 8 is:

```text
observed
not observed
common
rare
context-dependent
context-insensitive
recurrent
transient
robust
sensitive
suggestive
unresolved
```

Pass and fail remain appropriate for software, CI, validation, and execution contracts. They are not the vocabulary of a trajectory atlas.

The unconstrained system in Round 0 is baseline relational dynamics. It is not called a null hypothesis in this generation.

The model contains state, possible events, constraint weights, and stochastic event selection. Organisation, persistence, dissolution, reorganisation, return, recurrence, routing, context dependence, repair-like return, and boundary-like persistence may be observed afterwards. They are not encoded as a reward, a target, or a semantic goal.

Exploration decisions happen between rounds. No stochastic trajectory is rewarded for reaching a desired state. There is no optimisation against maximum routing divergence, entropy, organisation, or persistence.

Open exploration still requires a frozen round plan, bounded work, deterministic seeds, complete event provenance, replay, durable outputs, explicit branch decisions, and separate observation and inference. The difference from Mode A is the question, not the engineering.

A crisp distinction found here may later be isolated by a Mode A experiment on another branch. Generation 8 does not turn that isolation into an unbounded discriminating census inside this prompt. At most four rounds are executed: Round 0, Round 1, Round 2, and Round 3. The charter is `constraint-lab/exploration/generation-008/charter.md`.

## Information calibration

Whenever a descriptive information statistic is estimated from finite trajectories, first identify structural zero-information controls or exact-kernel comparators. Do not interpret the plug-in value directly when the estimator has a non-negligible finite-sample bias. Where the state space permits, prefer exact transition-law information to bias-corrected trajectory estimates.

This applies to later Mode A work and to later Mode B work.

A plug-in mutual information computed from a finite contingency table is one layer of the observation. A permutation of the labels, with the outcome marginals held fixed, estimates the finite-table bias of that same plug-in. An exact-kernel quantity, computed from the known transition law, is a third layer. The three layers answer different questions. A table names its layer.

Structural zero-information controls are part of the model. A system whose pair-event law does not read the triad is a calibration instrument for any statistic that claims triad-context information on the pair-event clock. If that statistic is large on the control, it is describing the estimator before it is describing the dynamics. The control is not a null hypothesis, and the comparison is not a pass/fail test.

Negative values of `observed plug-in − null mean` stay in the stored tables. They say the finite sample landed below the estimated null mean. Only an exact mutual information is mathematically non-negative. A float64 kernel result is a deterministic kernel result. It is not called a mathematical identity unless the arithmetic is exact.

## Mechanistic representation

After exploratory statistics identify a stable non-zero structure, search for a minimal mechanistic representation before expanding the experiment. Prefer a small exact causal geometry inside the explicit model transition law over repeated measurement of the same effect. The phrase "causal geometry" here means a dependence in that declared law. It is not, without a further qualification, a claim about a system outside the model.

## Finding dimensions

A finding has several dimensions. Magnitude, robustness, persistence, explanatory reach, and structural role must not be collapsed into a single strength score. A small or fragile phenomenon may be structurally essential. A large robust phenomenon may be mechanistically generic. Preserve the literal observation and let later relational evidence establish significance.

The coherence ledger is `constraint-lab/coherence/`. `findings.jsonl` and `relations.jsonl` are the record. The Markdown and Mermaid views are generated. A substantive generation appends findings and relations, regenerates the views, and writes an immutable snapshot under `constraint-lab/coherence/snapshots/`. The snapshot hash belongs in that generation's provenance. Future prompts name the coherence nodes that motivated them.

# Interpretation boundaries

## Inside the formal system

The following are mathematical statements about the Generation 1 kernel, and the tests lock the ones that are theorems of this engine.

- The baseline on `M > 0` toggles is uniform, irreducible, and period 2, with uniform stationary distribution and entropy rate `log2(M)` bits. At `M = 1` the entropy rate is 0.
- Any strictly positive weight list at `N = 2` normalises to the baseline kernel. Soft constraints on a single toggle are observationally null.
- A zero factor is the only Generation 1 operation that changes the support. Positive factors change measures on the same hypercube.
- For a fixed integer grade assignment and any base `r > 1`, the modal toggle set is independent of `r`. Support is independent of `r`. Magnitudes depend on `r`.
- Halt completion is a self-loop used for Markov analysis. It is flagged and is not a relational toggle.

These statements do not, by themselves, say anything about the ontology of reality.

## Inference

An inference says that a pattern in the observations is stable under the variations the cell actually performed: relabelling, the geometric alphabets, the declared horizons. A pattern that appears at one arbitrary factor and disappears at the neighbouring alphabet is reported as parameter-fragile. A pattern that is only a rephrasing of the baseline is reported as baseline-equivalent.

Inferences live in the generation report. They are not written back into motif files. A motif file carries the observed sentence, the coordinate, and an explicit note that inference and speculation are kept in the report. That split is there so a later reader can see the measurement without inheriting a name.

## RS / design interpretation

An interpretation asks whether an inferred pattern is coherent with the working premises in the charter, and with other relational findings, including findings in the archived programme. It may decrease local coherence, decrease global coherence, or leave the question open. It may notice a tension. It does not certify the premises.

Useful questions at this level, after a census exists:

- Does the same abstract motif recur on a second substrate (graph, hypergraph, simplicial complex, a later embedding)?
- Does the motif reduce the number of assumptions needed to describe several behaviours?
- Does it depend on an arbitrary numerical grade?
- Does a higher-order description subsume several lower-order observations?
- Does it illuminate an older RS word — closure, boundary, admissibility, dissolution, transformation, persistence — or does it pull against that word?

A boundary, if the word is used, has to be earned by an operational pattern such as high internal relational persistence together with low cross-cut transition probability. The engine has no object called a boundary.

## Constructive dissolution

The phrase names an interpretive candidate:

```text
organisation
→ pattern completion
→ relation dissolution
→ released possibility
→ reorganisation
```

The rise-then-release path measure is a weak, neutral shadow of the middle of that sequence (occupation rises by at least 2, then falls by at least 1). It is not the sequence itself. The baseline hypercube already produces a large rise-then-release probability. Only the excess over the baseline is evidence of a constraint effect. If a generation’s excesses are small, or are explained entirely by “prohibit some toggles, and the walk is pushed onto the remaining ones”, the report says that the candidate did not appear as a distinct motif, and it names the smallest extra literal that would make the question expressible. The original cell is not retuned afterward.

## Global coherence

A local pattern that is elegant inside one cell and that conflicts with the wider frame is recorded as a tension. A modest pattern that joins several disconnected observations may be the more useful result. The laboratory does not optimise the catalogue for a striking example.

# Literature map

The ontology is not taken from these sources. Each entry records a mathematical tool, the assumptions that come with it, what this laboratory does not inherit, and why the tool is useful. Page numbers are given only where the citation was checked closely enough to rely on them. Otherwise the entry names the work and the year.

## Finite Markov chains

**Levin, Peres, Wilmer, *Markov Chains and Mixing Times*.**  
Tool: irreducibility, period, stationary distribution, total variation, mixing.  
Assumptions: a time-homogeneous kernel on a countable state space.  
Not inherited: ergodic theorems are not read as claims about physical equilibrium. A point-mass start on a period-2 chain does not converge in total variation; the laboratory says so, and uses Cesàro language where that is the true statement.  
Useful because every Generation 1 grammar is a finite kernel.

**Kemeny and Snell, *Finite Markov Chains*.**  
Tool: absorbing classes, fundamental matrix, first-step analysis.  
Assumptions: finite state space, stationary transitions.  
Not inherited: the narrative of “absorption as the end of a process” in applied models. Halt is a completion we flag.  
Useful for hitting and absorption bookkeeping once a prohibit cuts the hypercube.

**Cover and Thomas, *Elements of Information Theory*; Shannon, “A Mathematical Theory of Communication”, 1948.**  
Tool: entropy rate of a stationary process, `−Σ_i π_i Σ_j P_ij log P_ij`.  
Assumptions: the chain is started in stationarity, or the rate is the asymptotic per-step entropy.  
Not inherited: an identification of entropy rate with thermodynamic entropy, or with uncertainty about the world.  
Useful as a single comparable number for how sharply a grammar concentrates the toggle choice.

## Symbolic dynamics and forbidden patterns

**Lind and Marcus, *An Introduction to Symbolic Dynamics and Coding*, 1995.**  
Tool: shifts of finite type; a local forbidden list defines a subshift.  
Assumptions: a fixed alphabet and a finite list of forbidden blocks, usually on a symbolic sequence.  
Not inherited: the identification of our relational state with a one-dimensional symbolic sequence. Our “forbidden” object is a transition of a hypercube, not a word in a shift space.  
Useful because a hard constraint (`weight = 0`) is exactly a local rule that deletes transitions, and the support graph is the resulting subshift’s analogue.

## Canonical labelling

**McKay and Piperno, “Practical graph isomorphism, II”, *Journal of Symbolic Computation* 60 (2014) 94–112. DOI 10.1016/j.jsc.2013.09.003. arXiv:1301.1493.**  
Tool: nauty/Traces canonical labelling and automorphism groups.  
Assumptions: the input is a coloured graph, and the goal is a canonical form under graph isomorphism.  
Not inherited: the software, in this generation. For `N ≤ 5`, `|S_N| ≤ 120`, and exact permutation tables are short enough to test by orbit enumeration.  
Useful as the tool to adopt when `N` leaves the range where `S_N` can be listed, or when the object being canonicalised is no longer a complete pairwise state.

## Higher-order relations

**Battiston, Cencetti, Iacopini, Latora, Lucas, Patania, Young, Petri, “Networks beyond pairwise interactions: structure and dynamics”, *Physics Reports* 874 (2020) 1–92. DOI 10.1016/j.physrep.2020.05.004.**  
Tool: the distinction between a graph, a hypergraph, and a simplicial complex, and the dynamical systems written on each.  
Assumptions: many of the reviewed models put a process on a fixed higher-order topology (contagion, synchronisation, diffusion).  
Not inherited: those particular dynamical models, and the assumption that the higher-order relation is static while a node state moves. In this laboratory the relation *is* the state, and constraints reweight changes of relation.  
Useful because it is the cleanest public statement of the distinction the semantics axis is required to keep.

**Battiston and coauthors, “The physics of higher-order interactions in complex systems”, arXiv:2110.06023.**  
Tool: a shorter map of the same territory.  
Assumptions: as above. A journal version is not cited here, because this note was written against the preprint.  
Not inherited: the physical modelling programme.  
Useful as a second entry point that does not collapse hypergraphs into simplicial complexes.

**Iacopini, Petri, Barrat, Latora, “Simplicial models of social contagion”, *Nature Communications* 10 (2019) 2485.**  
Tool: a concrete simplicial interaction.  
Assumptions: contagion on a fixed simplicial complex; nodes carry an infection state.  
Not inherited: the contagion rule, and the fixed complex.  
Useful later, as a comparison target, if a simplicial cell is opened. It is not a template for Generation 1.

## Random graphs, motifs, adaptive networks

**Milo, Shen-Orr, Itzkovitz, Kashtan, Chklovskii, Alon, “Network motifs”, *Science* 298 (2002).**  
Tool: the idea of a small subgraph pattern that recurs above a stated null model.  
Assumptions: the null is typically a degree-preserving randomisation of a fixed observed network.  
Not inherited: that null. Our baseline is the uniform hypercube walk, which does not preserve degree. A motif here is a constraint grammar, not an over-represented subgraph of one dataset.  
Useful as a warning about what “motif” already means in the literature, so the catalogue does not silently switch meanings.

**Robins, Pattison, Kalish, Lusher, “An introduction to exponential random graph (p*) models for social networks”, *Social Networks* 29 (2007).**  
**Snijders, Pattison, Robins, Handcock, “New specifications for exponential random graph models”, *Sociological Methodology* 36 (2006).**  
Tool: exponential families of graph distributions; local configuration statistics with parameters.  
Assumptions: a distribution on graphs, often with a near-degeneracy problem when parameters push the mass onto a few extreme graphs.  
Not inherited: the social-network interpretation, and the estimation-from-data setting.  
Useful because a soft constraint in this laboratory is morally a local reweighting of a graph distribution, and the ERGM literature is the place where that reweighting is known to be capable of degenerating. Halt and near-absorbing corners are the corresponding phenomena here, and they are recorded rather than fitted away.

**Maslov and Sneppen, “Specificity and stability in topology of protein networks”, *Science* 296 (2002).**  
Tool: degree-preserving rewiring as a null.  
Assumptions: a fixed degree sequence on a simple graph.  
Not inherited: the null itself. The Generation 1 baseline toggles any edge and changes degrees freely. Degree-preserving rewiring is a later comparison kernel, not the unconstrained substrate.  
Useful so that a future “null model” discussion does not quietly replace `μ₀`.

**Gross and Blasius, “Adaptive coevolutionary networks: a review”, *Journal of the Royal Society Interface* 5 (2008).**  
**Cimini, Squartini, Saracco, Garlaschelli, Gabrielli, Caldarelli, “The statistical physics of real-world networks”, *Nature Physics* 15 (2019).**  
Tool: networks whose edges and whose node states co-evolve; ensembles of real networks.  
Assumptions: usually an embedding in a domain model (epidemic, game, regulatory net) with its own rates.  
Not inherited: those domain rates.  
Useful later, when `S > 0` gives entities a channel that co-evolves with the relations.

## Rewriting, closure, constraints on constraints

**Danos and Laneve, “Formal molecular biology”, *Theoretical Computer Science* 325 (2004).**  
Tool: Kappa calculus; site-graph rewriting with local rules.  
Assumptions: agents have sites, and rules are chemical.  
Not inherited: the molecular ontology. The archived programme already explored molecules; this laboratory does not start there.  
Useful as one existing calculus in which a local rule changes a relational complex, including by deletion.

**Tarski, “On the calculus of relations”, *Journal of Symbolic Logic* 6 (1941).**  
Tool: relation algebra.  
Assumptions: a Boolean algebra of binary relations with composition and converse.  
Not inherited: the claim that every higher-order fact reduces to an algebraic combination of binary relations. The hypergraph axis exists because that reduction is exactly what must remain optional.  
Useful if a later DSL grows composition operators, and as a reminder that “relation algebra” already has a meaning.

**Maturana and Varela, *Autopoiesis and Cognition*, 1980. Mossio and Moreno, “Organisational closure in biological organisms”, *History and Philosophy of the Life Sciences* 32 (2010).**  
Tool: organisational closure as a name for a network of constraints that maintains the conditions of its own existence.  
Assumptions: a biological individual, and a philosophical account of function.  
Not inherited: the biological claim, and the decision to treat closure as a primitive of the grammar.  
Useful at the interpretation level, after a grammar is observed to regenerate the conditions that keep it active. Generation 1 has `L = 0` and cannot yet express a constraint maintaining a constraint.

**Feinberg, *Foundations of Chemical Reaction Network Theory*.**  
Tool: deficiency, complex balance, and the way a reaction graph constrains steady states.  
Assumptions: mass-action (or a relative) on species concentrations.  
Not inherited: species, concentrations, and mass-action.  
Useful later if a rate presentation replaces the embedded jump chain.

**Kauffman, “Metabolic stability and epigenesis in randomly constructed genetic nets”, *Journal of Theoretical Biology* 22 (1969). Mortveit and Reidys, *An Introduction to Sequential Dynamical Systems*.**  
Tool: Boolean networks and sequential dynamical systems; local rules, global attractors.  
Assumptions: a fixed wiring and a synchronous or ordered update of node states.  
Not inherited: the fixed wiring. Here the wiring is the state.  
Useful as a comparison once `S > 0` gives each entity a bit and the relations are the dependency graph.

## Path ensembles

**Redner, *A Guide to First-Passage Processes*, 2001.**  
Tool: first-passage and hitting times.  
Assumptions: usually a Markov process with an absorbing target.  
Not inherited: a privileged target state. The laboratory does not designate “the triangle” or “the empty graph” as the success state of the search.  
Useful when a later report asks how long a declared pattern takes to appear. That question has to be declared as a question, not built into the census.

**E and Vanden-Eijnden, “Transition-path theory and path-finding algorithms for the study of rare events”, *Annual Review of Physical Chemistry* 61 (2010).**  
Tool: ensembles of reactive trajectories between two sets.  
Assumptions: a reversible diffusion, or a Markov jump process, with designated reactant and product sets.  
Not inherited: the reactant/product split, and the molecular-dynamics setting.  
Useful once a motif has two operational sets worth connecting. Doob’s h-transform, which conditions a chain on hitting a set, is a related tool and is not used in Generation 1. Using it would change the measure under study; if it is used later, the conditioned kernel must be labelled as conditioned.

## Probability as reweighting

**Jaynes, “Information theory and statistical mechanics”, *Physical Review* 106 (1957).**  
Tool: maximum entropy subject to constraints, as a way to choose a measure.  
Assumptions: the constraints are expected values, and the prior is specified.  
Not inherited: the claim that the physical ensemble *is* the maximum-entropy distribution, and the use of that claim as an ontological argument.  
Useful because our soft constraints are a declared reweighting, which is the same mathematical gesture, aimed at transitions rather than at a static ensemble.

**Richardson and Domingos, “Markov logic networks”, *Machine Learning* 62 (2006) 107–136.**  
Tool: first-order formulae as weighted constraints on a Markov network.  
Assumptions: a grounded graphical model, trained or hand-weighted, usually for prediction.  
Not inherited: learning weights from data, and the closed-world database interpretation.  
Useful as a neighbouring language in which “formula ⇒ weight” is already formal. Our DSL is smaller and is enumerated rather than learned.

**Ashby, *An Introduction to Cybernetics*, 1956.**  
Tool: requisite variety; a regulator has to have enough internal variety to meet the variety of disturbances.  
Assumptions: a regulator/disturbance split.  
Not inherited: that split, and the managerial reading.  
Useful at the interpretation level if a constraint grammar is later seen to be small relative to the state space it organises. It is not a Generation 1 statistic.

## Event sourcing

**Fowler, “Event Sourcing”, 2005 (martinfowler.com).**  
Tool: persist the sequence of events, and treat current state as a fold over that sequence.  
Assumptions: a software system whose audit log is the source of truth.  
Not inherited: the enterprise-application setting.  
Useful because a trajectory in this laboratory is the research object. Replay is the test that the fold is deterministic.

## Constructive deletion

Quotients, matroid deletion and contraction, and negative design in self-assembly all treat removal as a structure-forming operation. They are analogies. The laboratory does not import matroid axioms or a chemical designer. They are listed so that “deletion can be generative” is recognised as an existing mathematical idea, which makes it safer to notice the phenomenon in a census and less tempting to hard-code it as a primitive.

## Deferred libraries

XGI, HyperNetX, and GUDHI become relevant when a hypergraph cell or a simplicial cell is actually executed. They are not dependencies of Generation 1. Stochastic hybrid systems, with a continuous state and a discrete mode, wait until `S` or `G` introduces a continuous coordinate. Using them earlier would smuggle a geometry or a clock into a pre-geometric cell.

# Observables

Observables describe the kernel and the paths it assigns positive probability. The names below are structural.

## Light observables (every canonical set)

- Deadlock states: admissible set empty, halt completion in force.
- Recurrent classes and their periods.
- How many recurrent classes are reachable from the empty state.
- Maximum and mean absolute one-step change in dissolution probability relative to the baseline `m/M`, skipping deadlock states (a halt has no dissolution probability).
- Closing bias, only when `M = 3`. On each of the three states with exactly two edges present, measure the probability of forming the missing edge. The baseline value is `1/3`. The bias is the mean of those three probabilities, minus `1/3`. A two-edge deadlock contributes 0.
- Whether the support map equals the baseline support map. Strictly positive weights leave the full hypercube support. Only a zero factor removes an edge of that graph.
- Modal map: at each state, the toggles of maximal weight, ties kept, or `halt`. The modal family hash is the hash of that map. A combined family id also folds in the support hash, so two grammars that share a mode map and differ by a prohibition land in different families.

## Heavy observables

Computed for every singleton, and for the first-seen member of every family.

- Long-run occupancy from the empty state, mixed across reachable recurrent classes by absorption weights.
- Mean edge density, edge-count occupancy, mean number of connected components.
- Entropy rate, in nats and in bits.
- Total variation of the long-run occupancy from the uniform measure.
- Reversibility defect: the largest absolute imbalance of stationary flow across a single toggle and its reverse.
- Halt mass.
- For `N = 3`, mass on the complete triangle (state 7). The baseline value is `1/8`.
- For `N = 4`, mass on the three perfect matchings, states `33`, `18`, and `12` in lexicographic edge order (edges `01+23`, `02+13`, `03+12`). The baseline value is `3/64`.
- Rise-then-release probability, from the empty state, over horizon `T` (the specification field `rise_release_horizon`), only when the labelled state count is at most 64. A path matches when its edge-count sequence has indices `i < j < k` with `count[j] ≥ count[i] + 2` and `count[k] ≤ count[j] − 1`. The reported excess is this probability minus the same probability on the baseline. The baseline already has substantial mass on such paths, because the hypercube walk rises and falls.

At `m = 0` the baseline forms with probability 1. At `m = M` the baseline dissolves with probability 1. A density-dependent reweighting can separate from the baseline only at intermediate occupation, or by changing which intermediate states are reachable.

## Screens

The specification declares three thresholds before the run. They are flags, not discoveries. Generation 1 uses:

```text
max |dissolution shift|  ≥ 0.1
|closing bias|           ≥ 0.1
|rise-then-release excess| ≥ 0.05
```

A weak favour already moves some toggle probabilities by more than 0.1, so the shift screen is coarse. Reports quote the histogram of the shift, not only the count of families that cross the flag. The rise-excess screen uses the family exemplar. The shift and closing screens use the range across the whole family.

## Families

A family gathers canonical sets with the same `N`, the same modal map, and the same support map. Tags:

- `baseline-equivalent` — the successor list equals the baseline successor list;
- `structural` — the support is a proper subgraph of the hypercube;
- `measure` — full support, kernel not identical to the baseline;
- `screened` — a predeclared flag fired, and the family is not baseline-equivalent.

A family may carry both `structural` and `screened`, or both `measure` and `screened`.

## Trajectory observables stored on an exemplar

For each event: state before, candidates, baseline weight, matching constraint factors, resulting weight, normaliser, integer draw, selected toggle or halt, state after. The run id hashes the engine version, specification hash, constraint-set id, initial state, PRNG name, seed, and horizon.

## What is deliberately not an observable

No score named for construction, repair, sacrifice, inversion, or self-transformation is computed. Component count, matching mass, triangle mass, halt mass, and the rise-then-release excess are the quantities from which a later interpretation may or may not propose those names.

# Research charter

## Purpose

The laboratory accumulates a reproducible catalogue of constraint motifs and the relational behaviours they generate. The working loop is:

```text
explore → observe → infer → compare → update coherence → ask the next question
```

The programme studies a formal system. A theorem inside that system is a theorem about the system. It is a separate act to ask whether the formal system is coherent with the wider Relational Substrate ontology.

## Working premises

These premises are upstream of the laboratory. The experiments do not try to establish them.

1. Reality is designed.
2. The observable creaturely/material runtime is not ontologically exhaustive.
3. The ultimate receiver in the deepest T–C–R sense may be non-material.
4. The non-material realm is not something this computational laboratory can directly access or simulate.
5. The laboratory therefore studies accessible relational/runtime effects and asks what kinds of architecture are coherent with the wider ontology.

The methodology is conditional:

> Assuming the overarching metaphysical frame, what relational runtime architecture follows coherently, and what can we learn by systematically exploring its possible constraint grammar?

A striking simulated trajectory is an observation inside the formal system. It is not an argument of the form “interesting simulated behaviour, therefore Designer.” The Designer premise is already in force. The laboratory is reverse engineering under that premise.

## Three levels

Every written result keeps these levels apart.

| Level | Question it answers |
| --- | --- |
| Observation | What did the formal model or the sampled trajectory do? |
| Inference | What recurring mathematical or relational pattern does that observation suggest? |
| RS / design interpretation | How might that pattern sit inside the wider ontology, under the working premises? |

T–C–R, closure, boundary, admissibility, and the archived physical models (nematic `RP²`, vortons, molecular descriptors, prior closure scores) may be named in the interpretation level after a result exists. They are not primitive objects of the grammar.

## What a constraint is

A constraint is a transformation of relational possibility. It modifies the measure over otherwise possible transitions. Persistence, exclusion, permeability, release, oscillation, fission, fusion, and patterns not yet named are possible consequences. Those words are not encoded as search targets.

The exploratory analogy is:

```text
relational possibility     ≈ alphabet / operating possibility
constraints                ≈ grammar
stochastic transition      ≈ execution semantics
trajectory                 ≈ expression
emergent organisation      ≈ runtime effect
```

The analogy guides questions. It is not an identity the implementation is required to enforce.

## Exhaustion before depth

Each generation declares a coordinate

```text
E(N, A, O, G, S, H, K, L; semantics, W, T, R)
```

and exhausts that cell. “Exhaustive” means every canonical object in the declared grammar was visited, and the coverage manifest counts labelled objects, objects removed by syntax, objects removed by symmetry, and the regions deliberately left unsearched. A Monte Carlo trajectory is a path through a known possibility space when the chain is finite and fully analysed. It is not itself an exhaustive census.

When a neighbouring cell is too large, the laboratory calculates its size, keeps the exact census of the shallower cell, and labels any sample as a sample.

## Neutrality of outcomes

The engine measures transition structure, occupancy, entropy rate, and path shape. Names such as constructive dissolution, boundary inversion, sacrificial persistence, and stochastic self-transformation are available only after a pattern has been observed, and only in the interpretation level. If a generation does not produce a candidate pattern, the report says so and names the smallest extra expressive capacity that would be required to ask the question again.

## Catalogue

The catalogue keeps null grammars, baseline-equivalent grammars, fragile parameters, absorbing deadlocks, and unexpected symmetries together with any distinctive motif. Evaluation, when used, is a vector of separate dimensions (reproducibility, coverage, parameter robustness, symmetry robustness, cross-substrate recurrence, trajectory distinctiveness, interpretability, global-coherence relevance). Those dimensions are not collapsed into a single score.

## Relation to the archive

`archive/pre-constraint-lab-2026-10-03/` preserves the earlier modelling programme. Archival is a historical boundary. It is not a repudiation. The new laboratory begins underneath geometry, particles, and the earlier closure scores. Later generations may use archived constructions as comparison targets.

# Scientific plan discipline

Before a scientific plan is frozen, execution tests may validate plumbing,
synthetic fixtures, serialization, canonicalisation and failure handling, but
they should not calculate representative scientific cells from the actual round.
If actual scientific cells must be used for calibration or timing, their exposure
must be declared and the final plan must distinguish pre-observed cells from
genuinely unopened cells.

Generation 8E declared K3-00 as a pre-freeze smoke test, K3-00 and K3-03 in unit
tests, and algebra items in unit tests. Review 008E notes that its external prompt
had already declared the question, formulas, counts, candidate values and
constructions. This policy is a methodological refinement, not a correction of
the E0 scientific results.

For F0, target/comparator specifications, symbolic local formulas, deterministic
80-digit roots, reference multipliers, canonical law fingerprints and counts
are frozen before scientific kernels. The polarity prerequisite is proved from
the baseline state mapping without running F0 kernels. After freeze, full-kernel,
epoch and stationary conjugacy are checked numerically before bridge execution.
Historical or synthetic laws supply timing and propagation tests. Tests of actual
F0 outputs are only invoked after the frozen commit has been pushed.

Execution checks the committed plan bytes and remote ancestry. Durable atomic
law items cache full and epoch kernels by law fingerprint, analysis version and
precision; items have a 120-second watchdog, resumable state and status/heartbeat.
Scientific results never enter plan construction. All tolerances are fixed in
the plan before results. Failures halt the affected analysis for debugging or an
explicit amendment; they do not select a different comparator or target.

## Formal integration and compilation gate (Generation 8G)

Before introducing a new ontology axis, ask:

> Can the proposed new behaviour be compiled into the existing ontology by increasing K, rule cardinality J, or explicit current state?

# Simplicial semantics — design note, not a result

Generation 3 executed independent hypergraph semantics. This note does not choose a simplicial dynamics, and it does not report a simplicial run.

A 2-simplex on `A`, `B`, and `C` is not the bit used in Generation 3. In this laboratory a simplex carries its faces. The independent triad does not.

These are separate design questions. An implementation has to answer each one. Leaving one implicit would compile a simplex into the hypergraph bit, which Generation 3 refuses.

1. How is formation of the simplex represented? Is it one event, or a derived label on a state that already has the three faces?
2. Does forming the simplex create faces that were absent?
3. Is formation prohibited unless all three faces are already present?
4. Does deleting a face delete the simplex?
5. Is dissolution of the simplex an event of its own, or only a consequence of losing a face?

Each answer is a different kernel. For example, automatic face creation is not the same rule as prohibiting formation until the faces exist, and neither is the same as deleting the simplex when one face is deleted. Generation 3 does not pick among them.

A later simplicial cell should name the answers in its specification before any shard runs. The comparison with Generation 3, if it is made, should use the same `N`, the same weights, and the pairwise conditional jump kernel, so a change of support or of reducibility can be attributed to face-closure rather than to a larger grammar.
